'''Charmaine B. Dean''' (born 1958) is a statistician from [[Trinidad]].{{r|westapp}}
She is the vice president for research at the [[University of Waterloo]],
a professor of statistical and actuarial sciences at both Waterloo and [[University of Western Ontario|Western University]],
the former president of the Western North American Region of the [[International Biometric Society]],
and the former [[President of the Statistical Society of Canada]].
Her research interests include [[Longitudinal study|longitudinal studies]], [[survival analysis]], [[Spatiotemporal database|spatiotemporal data]], [[heart surgery]], and [[wildfire]]s.{{r|dcd}}

==Education and career==
Dean was born in [[San Fernando, Trinidad and Tobago]] in 1958 and moved to Canada when she was 19.{{r|crmssc}}
She graduated in 1980 with honours in mathematics from the [[University of Saskatchewan]]. She did her graduate studies at the [[University of Waterloo]], earning a master's degree in 1984 and a Ph.D. in 1988,{{r|westapp}}
supervised by Jerry Lawless.{{r|mgp}} Her dissertation was ''Mixed Poisson Models and Regression Methods for Count Data''.{{r|crmssc|diss}}

After a year at the [[University of Calgary]],{{r|crmssc}}
she joined the faculty at [[Simon Fraser University]] in 1989, and became the founding chair of the Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science there at its establishment in 2001.{{r|westapp}}
She served as president of the [https://www.wnar.org Western North American Region] of the [[International Biometric Society]] in 2002<ref>{{Cite web |title=WNAR of IBS - Leadership |url=https://www.wnar.org/Leadership#Presidents |access-date=2022-09-25 |website=www.wnar.org}}</ref> and of the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] in 2007.{{r|dcd}}
She became Burnaby Mountain Research Chair at Simon Fraser before moving to the [[University of Western Ontario]] as Dean of Science in 2011.{{r|westapp}}
She stepped down as Dean at Western and became vice president for research at Waterloo in 2017.{{r|watvp}}

==Recognition==
Dean was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2007,{{r|fasa}} and in 2010 she was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].{{r|dcd}}
She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]]{{r|isimem}} and a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|ims}}

In 2003, she won the CRM-SSC Prize in Statistics of the [[Centre de Recherches Mathématiques]] and the Statistical Society of Canada.{{r|crmssc}}
In 2012 she won the Trinidad & Tobago Canadian High Commission Award.{{r|dcd}}
She was awarded the Gold Medal of the Statistical Society of Canada in 2023.{{r|goldmedal}}
